subject: SableCo on-prem SLA: proposed responsibility matrix & exception request
messages:
From: Dana Morris <dana.morris@sableco.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: SableCo Legal <legal@sableco.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: On‑prem responsibility apportionment for SLA

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this. As we prepare for the private deployment at our HQ racks, our legal/security teams asked us to get an explicit responsibility matrix from Redwood for SLA coverage.

Key facts:
- We manage all on‑prem network switching, firewalls, and the edge routers; Redwood will run the inference fleet in our co‑located cages.
- We expect variable latency during our scheduled WAN maintenance windows and occasional NIC firmware updates that restart hosts.

Ask: Can Redwood provide an exception to the standard uptime SLO for incidents clearly caused by customer‑controlled infra, and propose a clear apportionment (i.e., which component is Redwood responsibility vs SableCo)? We also need to understand what telemetry/access is required for you to validate and exclude these incidents.

I've attached a short request summary. Happy to jump on a call this week — legal looped in here.

Best,
Dana Morris
VP, Platform Engineering
SableCo Inc.

[Attachment: SableCo-SLA-Request.pdf (PDF)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dana Morris <dana.morris@sableco.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: On‑prem responsibility apportionment for SLA

Hi Dana — thanks for the clear write‑up. We can absolutely put together a responsibility matrix and a proposed appendix to the Private Deployment SLA that enumerates customer‑controlled carveouts.

A few quick asks so our engineering and legal teams can scope the change:
- Can you share the runbook for NIC/firmware updates and the typical maintenance calendar?
- What monitoring/alerting can you grant us (read‑only) for the on‑prem network elements during go‑live windows? (e.g., SNMP traps, sFlow, or a telemetry endpoint)
- Any regulatory constraints on telemetry we should be aware of?

I'll loop in our infra and legal to draft an appendix that:
- Lists exclusions (customer network, customer‑managed hardware, third‑party ISP outages)
- Defines data/telemetry required for incident validation
- Proposes an uptime baseline with carveouts and corresponding credits should Redwood miss its non‑excluded SLOs

I'll follow up with a draft by Friday. CCing Vivek for feasibility and Laura for legal redlines.

-Karthik
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: SableCo apportionment — proposed approach

Team — internal thread to align before I send the appendix to SableCo legal. Notes below; please reply with objections or edits.

Summary proposal (high level):
- Candidate baseline SLO for Private deployment: 99.5% monthly availability for service (excludes customer‑initiated maintenance windows and confirmed customer‑network incidents).
- Exclusions we want to enumerate explicitly:
  • Customer network (switches, routers, ISP links)
  • Customer‑managed compute reboot/firmware updates causing host restarts
  • Any third‑party service (e.g., power at customer datacenter when not under Redwood control)
- Incident validation: Redwood will require one or more of the following to validate an exclusion: time‑stamped telemetry (SNMP/syslog), customer support ticket ID showing root cause, or packet captures for the window. If telemetry cannot be provided within 72 hours, we reserve the right to open a joint investigation and treat as undetermined for credit purposes.
- Credits: For incidents attributable to Redwood (not excluded), propose pro‑rated monthly credits starting at 5% for <99.5% and scaled up; we can refine numbers with Sales.
- Operational controls: Require a mutually agreed maintenance calendar and a 48‑hour notice for any planned maintenance that would affect availability. For emergency maintenance initiated by SableCo, we will treat as exclusion if they document impact.

Action items:
- Vivek: confirm that requiring read‑only telemetry endpoints (SNMP/syslog) and the 72‑hour window is operationally feasible for our on‑prem support teams. Also confirm fallback modes (e.g., cache warming, graceful degradation) we can offer during customer network instability.
- Laura: draft a short appendix (2 pages) capturing the responsibility matrix and the validation flow; include language for ambiguous incidents and proposed credit table placeholder.

If we can get this out by end of week, I will send to Dana and their legal team with attachments.

Thanks — Karthik

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dana Morris <dana.morris@sableco.com>, SableCo Legal <legal@sableco.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed responsibility matrix & appendix (draft)

Hi Dana / SableCo Legal — thanks for your patience. Attached is our initial draft appendix and a CSV responsibility matrix that maps component -> owner -> example telemetry. Highlights below: 

- Baseline: 99.5% monthly availability for the Redwood service when running in Private (on‑prem) mode.
- Exclusions (examples): customer network devices, customer‑managed host reboots/firmware updates, ISP outages outside Redwood control.
- Validation: To qualify an event as an exclusion, SableCo must provide one of the following within 72 hours: time‑stamped SNMP/syslog exports, a ticket from your ops portal showing the root cause, or pcap evidence. If evidence is unavailable, we will run a joint investigation; incident attribution may remain undetermined for credit eligibility.
- Credits: Proposed placeholder table included in appendix. We are open to adjusting dollar/percent bands in negotiations.
- Operational asks: mutual maintenance calendar, 48‑hour notice for planned changes, and a read‑only telemetry endpoint (preferred).

Next steps:
1) Can you review the attached appendix and responsibility matrix and flag any items you cannot provide (telemetry types, timelines, etc.)?
2) If accepted, we will integrate the appendix into the Private Deployment addendum and route for legal signoff (DocuSign link included).

Attachments: RDW-SLA-Appendix-SableCo-redline.pdf (redline of proposed appendix), responsibility-matrix-sableco.csv (component -> owner -> telemetry examples).

If helpful, we can do a 30‑minute call Monday to walk through the validation flow and telemetry requirements.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

[Attachment: RDW-SLA-Appendix-SableCo-redline.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: responsibility-matrix-sableco.csv (CSV)]
